articles.title: IJMS, Vol. 27, Pages 10813: Role of PTEN in Bone Homeostasis and Skeletal Disorders
articles.description: Phosphatase and tensin homolog deleted on chromosome 10 (PTEN) is a well-established tumor suppressor that negatively regulates the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) signaling pathway. In recent years, accumulating evidence has positioned PTEN as an important regulator of skeletal homeostasis. PTEN participates in multiple aspects of bone remodeling through extensive crosstalk with major signaling pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, bone morphogenetic protein (BMP)/SMA and MAD homolog (SMAD), and receptor activator of nuclear factor κ-B ligand (RANKL)/RANK. At the cellular level, PTEN exerts distinct functions by regulating the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells, osteoblast proliferation and activity, osteoclastogenesis, and chondrocyte homeostasis. Notably, PTEN does not act as a uniform inhibitor. For instance, PTEN attenuation promotes osteogenic differentiation in bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells, yet impairs osteogenesis in dental pulp stem cells. Dysregulation of PTEN has been implicated in a broad spectrum of skeletal disorders, including osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and delayed fracture healing. Accordingly, therapeutic strategies targeting the PTEN/PI3K/Akt signaling axis have shown promising potential in preclinical studies. This review is dedicated to promoting a thorough understanding of the signaling mechanisms of PTEN in skeletal homeostasis and aims to offer a theoretical foundation for forthcoming endeavors in both basic and clinical research within this domain.
